messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty: alert fired INC-99102 — hosted-inference-prod — sudden 5xx spike + request latency increase on model-serving. Escalation policy: primary -> secondary(5m) -> manager(10m).
pagerduty-bot: INC-99102 routed to primary on-call: alex
alex: ack. I'm on it. seeing a jump in 502s from model-server replicas in eu-west-2. starting surface triage. :rotating_light:
nina: tagged as secondary on-call, will standby for escalation.
alex: quick dump of failing log snippet: ```
2026-03-22T02:14:03Z model-server WARN: serialization error writing kv cache
2026-03-22T02:14:04Z model-server ERROR: mem_limit_exceeded: cannot allocate 256MB
2026-03-22T02:14:05Z system INFO: pod restart backoff
```
matt: that's similar to the memory leak trace we saw a few weeks ago. any recent config changes?
alex: rolled a runtime config at 01:50 to enable prefix-cache aggressive retention. suspect retention parameter is too high — pods accumulate large KV snapshots and hit OOM.
pagerduty-bot: Escalation: primary acknowledged but secondary did not acknowledge within 5m. Escalating to manager: rob
rob: I'm awake, joining bridge now. bridge: https://meet.company/bridge/INC-99102. ping me on mobile if I drop.
nina: sorry, missed the PD page; in DND on mobile due to travel. no ack. I'll pick up handoff if needed.
alex: taking immediate mitigations: pausing rollout, scaling down prefix retention, and rebalancing pods away from nodes with repeated OOMs. running commands: ```bash
kubectl set env deploy/model-server PREFIX_RETENTION=2 -n prod
kubectl rollout pause deploy/model-server -n prod
```
matt: adding an emergency route for high-importance customers to dedicated pool to avoid exposure: `route override --service model-serving --pool dedicated-highprio`
incidentbot: Customer impact: multiple hosted customers experiencing degraded generation latency and elevated error rates. Service degradation flagged for 12 customers (top 3 paid).
rob: priority: protect paid customers. approve reroute and short-term rollback of prefix-cache change. alex/matt proceed.
alex: rolling back canary config and draining three affected nodes. drain command: `kubectl drain ip-10-0-4-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
matt: confirmed reroute applied, traffic split 80/20 to backup pool for premium keys. monitoring SLOs.
alex: after rollback and drains, success rate improved from 71% -> 94% within ~9 minutes. still seeing occasional crashloops on oldest pods.
nina: can we push a hotfix that zeroes stale KV pointers on init? I have a small patch, but deployment requires quick smoke tests.
rob: authorize hotfix deploy to prod if smoke tests pass within 10m. we cannot leave unstable pods.
alex: smoke tests passed in staging. deploying hotfix to a gated canary 1/10. watch: `kubectl set image deploy/model-server model-server=registry/redwood:model-kv-fix-2026-03-22`
incidentbot: PagerDuty note: manager paged at 02:20 after secondary missed ack. bridge active. severity set to Sev2.
matt: hotfix canary healthy for 5 minutes; promoting to 4/10. overall error rate continues to decline.
nina: back from DND, joining bridge. I see the timeline. I'll take over monitoring for next 45m to ensure stability.
rob: thanks. please ensure postmortem with root cause and mitigations: revert risky retention defaults, add HPA memory limits, improve PagerDuty esc escalation to use SMS fallback, and add cross-region canary throttles.
alex: noted. opening incident ticket INC-99102 in tracker with preliminary notes and mitigation timeline.
matt: customer-ops notified: message sent to affected customers, offering ETA and mitigation summary.
incidentbot: Incident INC-99102 update: acknowledged by alex, escalated to rob (manager) after secondary missed ack, bridge active, partial traffic reroute in effect.
nina: taking over incident ownership for stabilization window. alex you can sign off and document handoff. :thumbsup:
alex: handing off to nina. logging a short ops note and signing out. thanks team.
rob: good coordination. follow-up: schedule postmortem and action items in 48h.
